notes.title: Sneak Peek Roundup - April Edition
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

If you’ve been hanging out in our Discord lately, you’ve probably seen a ton of bite-sized sneak peeks popping up. But if you missed them - or you're more of a Steam scroller - don’t worry! It’s time to round them all up and drop them here for your viewing pleasure. Let’s take a look at what we’ve been working on over the past few weeks in Ardem:

So, let’s round up another month's worth!

[hr][/hr]
[h3]#1 – Locked, Loaded, and... Kinda Sarcastic?[/h3]

We kicked things off with a new weapon in the works—the M14! It’s one of ten new guns coming to Ardem, and while it's technically for shooting robots... well, we’ll let your moral compass (and server rules) decide what really happens out there.

[img]https://playardem.com/images/roundup/april25/ROUNDUP_APRIL_M14_01.png[/img]

[h3]#2 – Custom Characters Are Coming[/h3]

The days of playing as "that one bald dude" are coming to an end. We shared our first look at the upcoming customisable character model - and yes, it’s still in progress, but we’re getting closer every day!

[img]https://playardem.com/images/roundup/april25/ROUNDUP_APRIL_MAYA_01.png[/img]

[h3]#3 – A New Place to Hold Down: The Prison[/h3]

During one of our bi-weekly team check-ins, we showed off Dini’s work on a new point of interest - the Prison! It’s got serious potential as a base location, but let’s just say... it’s not exactly move-in ready.
We’re always adding new places like this, and they’re shaping up to be big additions for future closed alpha testing.

[img]https://playardem.com/images/roundup/april25/ROUNDUP_APRIL_PRISON_01.png[/img]

[h3]#4 – The Character Creator Reveal[/h3]

🎉 It’s here! We shared a first look at Ardem’s in-progress Character Creator! 🎉
Our bald friend has served us well, but it’s time to pass the torch. This system’s still in development, but you can now see where it’s headed - and yes, it’s as cool as you hoped.

[img]https://playardem.com/images/roundup/april25/ROUNDUP_APRIL_CHARACTER_01.gif[/img]

[h3]#5 – Fully Customised, Fully In-Game[/h3]

Right after the Character Creator reveal, we followed up with something even better: a character, fully customised and already exploring the world of Ardem. And yes, there’s hair! It exists!
We’re also experimenting with clothing customization, so stay tuned - more on that soon. 👕

[img]https://playardem.com/images/roundup/april25/ROUNDUP_APRIL_CHARACTER_02.gif[/img]

[h3]#6 – A Bittersweet Farewell + Scope GIF Time[/h3]

We said goodbye to Chris, our community wizard, who helped build so much of the friendly tone you know and love. We’re wishing him all the best in his new adventure, and we’re incredibly thankful for his time with us. With that said, Phillip stepped in to take over the updates - and what better way to start than with a timelapse GIF of a new scope being modelled? One of many new attachments (and weapons) heading into the game!

[img]https://playardem.com/images/roundup/april25/ROUNDUP_APRIL_SCOPE_01.gif[/img]

[h3]#7 – Plot Antennas: They’re Here, They’re Glorious[/h3]

Plotpoles just got a massive upgrade—literally. Say hello to the new Plot Antennas!
We’re introducing five stages of upgradeable antennas, each expanding your building radius but also increasing maintenance needs. They require new resources to build and keep running, so get ready to make some choices on how you invest in your base’s future. 📡

[img]https://playardem.com/images/roundup/april25/ROUNDUP_APRIL_ANTENNAS_01.jpg[/img]

And that’s a wrap on this month’s Sneak Peek Roundup!

If you want to catch these updates as they happen, jump into the Ardem Discord - it’s where we drop all the little behind-the-scenes bits and chat directly with the community.

Thanks for following along, and as always...

See you in Ardem!

— The Techtive Games Team

notes.title: The Open Alpha will REMAIN OPEN!
notes.content:
Hey, everyone!

We’ve been blown away by the response to the Open Alpha! We’ve been getting a ton of feedback, squashing bugs we didn’t even know about and having fun jumping in and playing with people. It’s with that in mind that we’ve made a decision…

We’re keeping the Alpha [b]OPEN! [/b]

We may close it as we get closer to our Early Access launch but for now, the gates are staying open!

We hope you stick with us on this journey as we work towards making the game we all want to play!

See you in Ardem, 

- Techtive Games

notes.title: Design Competition Winner
notes.content:
Hello, everyone!

You may recall a month ago we launched our [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2179480/view/507319906279097132?l=english]Design Competition[/url] over on our [url=http://discord.gg/ardem]Discord[/url]. We have read all the entries and considered all the options, but we have finally chosen the winner!

[b]Congratulations, elizarya, for coming up with the winner! [/b]

[quote=elizarya]"A drive in theatre could be fun maybe. You could even have it able to play a movie if you wanted  Theres a survival game I am playing and in it you have a stress level you have to manage, and one of the ways to destress is that you can put a DVD disk of "Night of the living dead" in your TV and actually watch the entire movie in game. That movie is in the public domain so there are no copyright issues to using it if you decided the theatre should work and actually play a movie for fun. There are other pub domain movies also so you could even have finding new movie reels to play/collect be a thing. You could go for irony and do "It's a wonderful Life" lol. Of course if you did that it'd have to have a big non-relocatable generator that runs the place so the projector works, and you could add some gas to it. Otherwise some abandoned cars, a concession stand, maybe some lawn chairs and beer coolers and littered popcorn boxes scattered around the parking area past the ticket booth at the entry to the driveway...?"[/quote]
We have already reached out on Discord to let them know they are now in the closed alpha program, will receive a key for the early access release and we will name the cinmea after them (unless they want a different name).

We will get to work on this right away, but we don't have a build ETA just yet. No doubt, though, you're going to see it in sneak peeks! 

We also want to say a HUGE thank you to all the other entries! 

[b]Thank you all again SO much! [/b]We will 100% be running more things like this in the future! 

- See you in Ardem!

notes.title: Sneak Peek Roundup #2
notes.content:
Hello, everyone!

If you caught our last Sneak Peek Roundup you’ll know the deal. But just in case, [url=http://discord.gg/ardem]our Discord[/url] is the place to be for a lot of our smaller updates. We have short videos and screenshots that give everyone an insight into what we’re working on right then. 

So, let’s round up another month's worth!
[hr][/hr]
[h3]#1 Into The Swamp[/h3]

[i]Text from the original post…[/i]

So, in the last sneak peek you saw the new area from high up, today we're taking a closer look!  

I took this screenshot in today's bi-weekly progress meeting with the team and it's your first look at the flooded swamp land that you will find in the new area we are working on. You can also get a sense, looking at the aerial view [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2179480/view/507318638682833169?l=english]above[/url], roughly where this flooded barn might be and get a sense of the scale we're trying to build in Ardem! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44384659/9e22f927aa516370ae362f80dfba828d200fa054.png[/img]

[h3]#2 Farms in the New Area[/h3]

[i]Text for the original post…[/i]

"[i]...it was when farms began to fail that we truly understood, nothing was going to be the same anymore.[/i]" - Survivor 217

It's another sneak peek at the new area we're building! This time it's an abandoned farm which you can stumble across. The whole area features a lot of what was previously farm land. Possibly great to build a new future on, possibly not. Time will tell. 

We love putting these points of interest into the game and trying to tell a little story just using the environment. Be sure to check back here next week as we may have some news on how you could get involved with that as well...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44384659/6fadd1a2ae679af341fe2bc105ce08ae15f4bace.png[/img]

[h3]#3 Corn with a C[/h3]

[i]Text from the original post…[/i]

"[i]I had no idea so much code went into Corn...[/i]" - Me, jumping in a meeting this morning.

Staying fed will be a big part of Ardem, and farming will be something a survivor can work towards! Maybe you'll be the Farmer on your server? Though, you'll probably need either some good defences, or some agreements with other clans to protect your crops. Or maybe you just stay a little more low key and just farm for yourself. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44384659/aff9dede658832f647a5844d3356d1a07bf68073.png[/img]

[h3]#4 The Fog Descends on the Swamp[/h3]

[i]Text from the original post…
[/i]
You may have seen the area in our latest dev diary, or some of the maps above, that feature a "swampy" terrain. Well, here we are experimenting with trying to bring that swamp atmosphere with some volumetric fog. We're not saying there's anything spooky in the swamp. 

We are not saying that. It just, I mean, it looks both spooky and chill at the same time, right?!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44384659/69a95232d15aef06a8c9a037af515e978bcf6266.png[/img]

[h3]#5 When the Trees Fly[/h3]

[i]Text from the original post…[/i]

Not so much a sneak peak, it's a fun bug we found while play testing the other day. Should flying trees be a feature and not a bug?! No. But what if...?

No.  

[previewyoutube=sz_FUi6bE30;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]#6 The Road Ahead[/h3]

[i]Text from the original post…[/i]

"[i]Just follow the signposts, they should get you there. Unless someone has messed with the signposts, but nobody would do that, right?[/i]" - Survivor 0486

Hello everyone! It's another Sneak Peak for you, and you can see here, we're trying to make the world of Ardem as immersive as we can! We hope you can find where you need to go with signs, but hey, who knows what condition those signs are in. And how accurate they might be...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44384659/49f786fe45d004cbc27baa6a1ba1148814743184.png[/img]
[hr][/hr]
And that’s another month of sneak peeks from the [url=http://discord.gg/ardem]Ardem Discord server[/url]! If you want to see everything as soon as it comes out, be sure to join us! The team is there to chat about the game and it’s the best place to hear the second we open the Closed Alpha Testing or the date of our next Open Alpha Test!

Until next time, 

- Techtive Games

notes.title: Closed Alpha Roundup #1
notes.content:
Hello, everyone!

As you may have seen, a while back, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2179480/view/505063032913657896?l=english]we opened up applications[/url] to join us for a Closed Alpha. We had [i]a lot[/i] of applications and let in even more people than we planned because of it. One thing that has really been exciting for us is the amount of great screenshots and moments our testers have been sharing, so we thought we’d share some with you here!
[hr][/hr]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44384659/db0cb984a84b0636ca54f0f85e721c219134c7bd.png[/img]
This screenshot from Nanjan really shows off the more chill side of Ardem, out by the water fishing with a fellow survivor.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44384659/0262c8f73c330e972b7d21e4c5be9e3a77161525.png[/img]
Another from Nanjan, chilling later on watching the sunset. This makes Arderm look so peaceful! You could almost forget the killer robots, and the less friendly other players...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44384659/e2f79c3e799c8e67577db9c92a494a85cb531e5f.png[/img]
Here, we see the True Closed Alpha Tester experience as players ventured into the new part of the map for the first time. We’ve explored this area in our [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2179480/view/507319272300609650?l=english]latest Dev Diary[/url] Marick, who took this one and titled it “[i]Highway to Hell[/i].”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44384659/33d851c3af7cdde9d3aed3b4f3eec5a76510a1d8.png[/img]
Malrun took this while exploring. Honestly, we’re not sure what this is up there. “[i]UFO’s confirmed[/i]” was one comment. We can neither confirm nor deny this. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44384659/a96acee1845224f02c9ada0abf8fc99eb914227b.jpg[/img]

[hr][/hr]
The amount of bugs we’ve fixed, ideas people have come up with and fun we’ve had just during this first month of our closed alpha has been huge! We’re incredibly thankful to our team of closed testers!

We will have [b]another Open Alpha[/b] in the not too distant future, and we are [b]looking to re-open the closed alpha applications soon[/b]. So, be sure to keep an eye out here, or head to [url=https://discord.gg/dgv7HJ2hnV]our Discord[/url] to join the conversation! 

Until next time, 

- Techtive Games.

notes.title: Design A Part of Ardem!
notes.content:
Hello, everyone! 

Points of interest and environmental storytelling are a part of Ardem that is close to our hearts. We thought, wouldn't it be cool if you guys got to design one, and then we build it and put it in the game! 

[list]
[*] The area can't be too complicated, so "a theme park about me with 100 NPCs and fully working rollercoasters" is out for now. 
[*]It also has to fit into the post-apocalyptic world of Ardem. So, "a dragon nest" wouldn't really work, either.  But a lot *does* fit so you can still have fun.
[*] [b]We only need a written description[/b], no need to actually draw or design anything!
[*] Post your entries in our Discord in the Design-Comp channel.
[/list]
If you haven’t already, you can join our [url=https://discord.gg/dgv7HJ2hnV]Discord here[/url].

But that's it! We will pick our favourite entries and then the community will vote on which one they like the most! 

Can't wait to see what you come up with!

- Techtive Games

notes.title: Sneak Peek Roundup #1
notes.content:
Hello, everyone!

[url=https://discord.gg/dgv7HJ2hnV]Over on Discord[/url] we’ve been making small little development updates, which while they don’t need their own blog post, are still interesting little sneak peeks into the development of Ardem. We wanted to share a roundup of some of the more recent ones we have posted there and share them with you!
[hr][/hr]
[h3]#1 Character Model Updates[/h3]

[i]Text from the original post…[/i]

“We're making our own character models! This is the first of a few that will be added to Ardem! 

We're very excited to be adding the customisation many of you asked for in Open Alpha Test 3, so hopefully by the next Open Alpha (spoilers, there will be another), you'll be able to create your own survivor and roam Ardem meeting more unique people! “

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44384659/c7cfb8b96a509a096e5fc82dbe06e8b4f90e7dc0.png[/img]

[h3]#2 The Process of Making Sound
[/h3]
[i]Text from the original post…[/i]

Ever wondered what adding and testing sound in a game looks like? In our team meeting this morning, René showed us some of the work he has been doing and I was fascinated by the test world they had to see how it all works! 

Maybe we should take a look at more elements of building the game like this in future dev diaries? Let us know what kind of stuff you'd like to see more of! 

Side note, the Boars are no longer ninja boars, they have a range of sounds! No more sneak attacks!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44384659/1e2d824dc4098328fe1a0fafbc687f6afb2de39f.png[/img]

[h3]#3 Character Customization[/h3]

[i]Text from the original post…
[/i]
"When will we get to customise our character?" Well, I can tell you, we're working on it! 

Our first character model, which you can see here, is fully tested and other than a few animation issues we're pretty close to it being ready to go. This also means we can test out and start implementing the clothing system, which you can also see on the character model. 

Before we began this process, we had an artist make some explorations of what characters in Ardem could look like, which you can see in the second image.  We hope to get this system out to our Closed Alpha Testers as soon as we can!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44384659/46c36f16ce9d1e76342251df6ee79c9f9ea2b829.png[/img]

[h3]#4 A New Area of the Map[/h3]

[i]Text from the original post…[/i]

We hitched a ride with a UFO for this Sneak Peek!  

This area outlined in yellow is a whole new area the team have been working on since the last Open Alpha. It has a lot more of a rural, farmland vibe with a couple of farms inside. It's also a bit swampy as it's partly flooded. 

There is some urban life in there though, with a shopping mall, a vehicle dealership and an airstrip (Planes, in Ardem?!) so there will be a ton to explore and loot to gather. It may be a little while until we roll this area out to our @Alphatester gang but they will be the first to check it out!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44384659/52dcacf6b0cf90f549720a709781e8aa62a7e21f.png[/img]
[hr][/hr]
And that’s just the four most recent sneak peeks! We’ve been adding these for a good few months now so it’s worth [url=https://discord.gg/dgv7HJ2hnV]heading to our Discord[/url] to see some more as well as get the latest updates as they come out. Discord is also a great place to chat with the team and learn about future Alpha Tests early!

Until next time, 

- Techtive Games

notes.title: The Year Ahead for Ardem
notes.content:
Hello, everyone! 

2025 is here, and the team is back at work after the winter break. 2024 went by so fast, but we are really blown away by all the feedback, videos, and new faces that have joined us! Playtest 3 went really well, and we gained a ton of useful feedback from all of you! [b]Thank you![/b]

With that in mind, we're looking to the future! In the short term, applications are still open for our [b]Closed Alpha Program[/b]. If you [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2179480/view/505063032913657896?l=english]didn't read about it[/url], you can sign up, and if selected, you'll be able to test Ardem and join us for specific sessions where we will all test new systems and stress test our servers. [b]Applications will close on January 12th[/b], and selected participants will receive their keys on January 13th. We will also have a bunch of Dev Diaries going live, as well as some interesting new content, but more on that at a later date! 

In the long term, we are working towards our next Public Alpha Playtest, and while we don't have a locked-in date for that just yet, it isn't too far on the horizon! We will continue to share small updates and sneak peeks over on our [b]Discord server [/b]so be sure to [url=https://discord.gg/dgv7HJ2hnV]join us there[/url]! We are also aiming to see the game's Early Access launch this year, so 2025 will be a huge one for us! 

We can't wait to see you all again in Ardem, 

- Techtive Games

notes.title: Thank you for playing Alpha Test 3!
notes.content:
Hello, all!

notes.title: Getting Started Guide for Playtest 3
notes.content:
Welcome to the third Alpha Playtest for Ardem! Ardem is a third person, survival game so if you’ve not been in one of our playtests before, or if you’ve never played a survival game before, we’ve put together this little guide that should help get you started! 

This guide should get you to the point where you know what you’re doing and can begin to fend for yourself in the world of Ardem. There are many threats, from robots to other players. But there’s always the chance you might make a new friend and build, survive and thrive together in the ruins of society. 

It’s worth noting that the entire map is not available in this playtest as we are still actively working on the game so you will encounter walls as you play. Rest assured, this will not be in the final release.

If you find yourself stuck, or with any other questions about the game, please head to [url=https://discord.gg/ardem]our Discord[/url] where we, and the community, will be able to help you out! 

[h2]First Steps in Ardem[/h2]

[b]Spawn Location[/b]
As a new player, you’ll start on either the west or south coast, with spawn points scattered along the beaches. While each location has different distances to loot spots, the overall experience is similar.

[b]Gathering Basic Resources[/b]
The beaches are a great place to find driftwood and drift metal—essential for crafting tools early on. Tools can also be looted, but crafting lets you stay safe in the wild and avoid other players. You’ll need wood, metal, and rope. For rope, either search or craft it yourself using plant fibres. 

[list]
[*] [b]Fishing rod[/b]: Helps with food.
[*] [b]Bow and arrows[/b]: Good for defense.
[*] [b]Axe[/b]: Essential for firewood
[/list]
To bring up the crafting menu [b]press tab[/b] on your keyboard and head to the crafting menu. You’ll find most things you need in the tab menu! It’s worth noting that not all tools are craftable, many of them you’ll have to find in the world.

[b]Securing Food and Water[/b]
Early survival means ensuring you have enough food and water:

[list]
[*] [b]Water[/b]: Drink directly from rivers or lakes, find bottles to fill, or loot canned drinks.
[*] [b]Food[/b]: Find canned goods, gather forest berries, hunt fish or animals, and grill meat for higher nutrients. A grill grate is needed for proper cooking.
[/list]
[b]Night Preparation[/b]
Be ready for nightfall with your flashlight and spare batteries, which you will spawn with. Campfires are useful for visibility but remember that light and fires can be seen from a distance. If you don’t want other players to see you, be careful. Build fires with stones (found on roads or beaches), add wood, and use matches or a fire drill to ignite.

[b]Using Vehicles[/b]
Vehicles are excellent for fast travel but require fuel and maintenance. Use a gas canister or an empty bottle to siphon fuel from wrecks and salvage parts with a wrench. Keeping your vehicle in good shape is essential to avoid permanent damage.

[b]Building and Storage[/b]
As you gather loot, consider your storage options:

[list]
[*] [b]Storage boxes[/b]: Place them in a secure location.
[*] [b]Vehicles[/b]: Carry storage boxes for mobile loot.
[*] [b]Bases[/b]: Build a small base for safer storage.
[/list]
[b]Base Building Basics[/b]
To start building, find a hammer (available in industrial or residential areas) and open the build menu by pressing "X". In multiplayer, a plot pole is required first, located under the Misc category. Build frame walls first, and add wood, metal, or stone paneling by selecting them with a middle-click while holding the hammer.

[b]Electricity and Decoration[/b]
To add lighting, you’ll need a wire cutter. Use the Electricity category in the build menu to install power components and find fuses to manage circuits. Decorate with furniture and customize your base. You can take any furniture you find in the world, simply pick it up and it will be packed into a convenient box for you. But you will have to carry this box back, so a vehicle might be important.

[b]Farming[/b]
For a reliable food source, grow crops like tomatoes and eggplants by planting seeds on grassy or muddy ground, found in garages and sheds.

[b]Robot Dangers[/b]
Beware of robots patrolling high-risk areas like cities and military checkpoints. You can either avoid or flee from them when encountered. You may, however, find weapons, which can be used to take these robots out as well as protect yourself from others, if needed.
________

With this, you should be ready to get started in Ardem!

Most items can be found in places you might expect to find them. For example, car parts in a garage or food items in an abandoned homes kitchen. However, as we mentioned above, if you find yourself lost or confused, come and talk to us on [url=https://discord.gg/ardem]Discord[/url] and we can help you!

If you encounter any bugs, you can [b]press the * button[/b] which will let you add details and a screenshot. If you get stuck and just want to know what to do, please also let us know in Discord!

We hope you have as much fun playing as we have making this Alpha, thank you for joining us to test and shape the future or our first game!

- [b]Techtive Games.
[/b]

notes.title: Ardem - Dev Diaries [May]
notes.content:
[b]Don't forget to join our Discord to always get the latest news on updates and events![/b]

[url=https://discord.gg/ardem][img]https://playardem.com/images/devdiaries/ARDEM_Steam_Store_Discord_Banner_600x100_2.png[/img][/url]

[h1]Attention, survivors![/h1]

We are excited to provide you with detailed information on what has happened since the last dev diary a month ago. If you haven’t noticed, we have changed the dev diary cycle from biweekly to monthly to give us more time to work on the report and have more to show. This edition will be quite large, and we are super happy about the progress we have made. As always, give us a thumbs up if you like it and leave a comment if you have any questions. Let’s dive in!

[h2]Art[/h2]

On the art side we have worked on two major aspects of the game. 

As we continue to unify our flora and fauna to make them as authentic and realistic as possible, we have focused on leafed trees this time. As you might have noticed in the playtests, there was a noticeable discrepancy between the highly detailed conifers and the low-poly leafed trees, which made the scenes in mixed forests look a bit off. We have now replaced these legacy trees with a brand new set that matches the conifers in fidelity. Since vegetation is a major part of our level design, this has been an important step in enhancing the overall immersion when moving through Ardem, especially in dense forests.

The lion's share of the work went into the technical art of the trees, ensuring they properly react to wind and weather conditions and enabling players to chop them down. What might sound like the easy part actually involves a lot of work, including fine-tuning values and extensive testing until the visual appearance meets our expectations and blends seamlessly with our existing trees.

[img]https://playardem.com/images/devdiaries/Mai24/ARDEM_DEVDIARY_May24_Trees_02.gif[/img]

However, the level designers have already started working with the new trees and have fallen in love with them. It’s a nice change and offers an almost biome-like variety of flora in these new areas.

Many of you have been asking if there will be additional weapons, and the answer is - of course -“Yes!” The currently integrated weapons have been more of a placeholder to enable us to implement the weapon system and provide a means to defend yourself from enemy players or hostile animals. However, we have started working on the enhanced weapon system, which includes the first “real” weapons with attachments and more.

[img]https://playardem.com/images/devdiaries/Mai24/ARDEM_DEVDIARY_May24_Weapon_01.png[/img]

As Ardem is set in a fictional Midwest state of the US, we aim to depict reality as closely as possible, including the range of firearms you would find in such a state. When Ardem hits early access, you can expect a wide variety of guns and corresponding attachments to visually customize your weapons and improve certain attributes such as precision. More details on the enhanced weapon system will be covered in the programming section.

[h2]Leveldesign[/h2]

With the fresh air of new trees being implemented, our level designers went into ultra hyperfocus mode and managed to design nearly 7 square kilometers of the map within the last few weeks. This corresponds to almost 10% of the entire map size, marking the most significant level design progress we've made on the project so far and bringing us one step closer to closing the gap on the south coast of the map.

[img]https://playardem.com/images/devdiaries/Mai24/ARDEM_DEVDIARY_May24_Southcoast_01.png[/img]

The new area is full of unique and handcrafted points of interest, enabling players to explore and discover various places with their own stories. To provide players with more convenient guidance, we have added several landmarks and hiking trails that will lead them to key points on the map. With the new foliage in place, the entire area offers beautiful scenery with plenty of opportunities to hide and build hidden shelters in the dense leaf forests.

[img]https://playardem.com/images/devdiaries/Mai24/ARDEM_DEVDIARY_May24_Southcoast_02.png[/img]

We are super excited about the progress we have made over the past few weeks and would love to show as many points of interest as possible. However, the area is just too large, so we will share individual locations in the next dev diaries. As mentioned in the last dev diary, we have now finished the flooded area with the collapsed bridge. The result is amazing, and we can't wait for you to discover all the pathways and routes we've added around the bridge to ensure you don't get too wet.

[img]https://playardem.com/images/devdiaries/Mai24/ARDEM_DEVDIARY_May24_CollapsedBridge_01.png[/img]

Besides all that, we have been experimenting with rivers, as some of the playtest feedback clearly stated that the rivers in Ardem are too steep and not visually appealing. After some experimentation, we found a good workflow that offers a good balance between effort and fidelity. For steeper gradients, we will now use shorter water terraces connected by small waterfalls instead of one overly steep river. We are very pleased with the results and believe it enhances the overall aesthetics.

[img]https://playardem.com/images/devdiaries/Mai24/ARDEM_DEVDIARY_May24_Waterfall_01.png[/img]

So, as you can see, we are not only adding new places and pushing forward the general progress of the map, but we are also focusing on improving the aesthetics of the existing areas. We are committed to steadily enhancing the look and feel of the game.

[h2]Sounddesign[/h2]

Huge progress has been made on the sound side, where we have completed the new Ardem main theme that will be featured in the game's main menu. While the old song was more of a placeholder, meant to be found in-game, the new theme encapsulates all the emotions that we believe define Ardem. With the main theme in place, we can create different iterations for various purposes such as in-game music, tutorial ambient music, and more. We might share the theme song in one of the upcoming dev diaries, so keep an eye out!

We have also been working on sounds for many different object interactions, such as item consumption (eating and drinking), vehicle wreck doors, and tools like hammers, pickaxes, and saws, among many others. Next, we will be reworking all character footstep sounds to better represent the different ground materials in the game.

[h2]Programming[/h2]

On the technical side, we have been working on robot AI and have implemented a first version of the robots for in-game testing. Robots now spawn and despawn based on player proximity. Once spawned, they follow a certain idle behavior, such as patrolling an area, until they perceive player movement and switch into combat mode. There are different types of robots (military, security, police, medical, etc.) that will spawn depending on their location. For example, when you enter a hospital, police and medic robots will spawn, while heavily armed military robots will spawn in military camps and outposts. Higher-tier loot areas lead to more robot presence. Additionally, robots mostly spawn near urban areas and structures and are less likely to be found in highly rural areas. During testing, we found a couple of technical issues that we are now addressing before deploying the AI to the alpha tester branch for more in-depth testing.

[img]https://playardem.com/images/devdiaries/Mai24/ARDEM_DEVDIARY_May24_Robots_01.gif[/img]


The new enhanced weapon system has made significant progress over the last couple of weeks. We have taken a lot of feedback from the playtest into account, and the range of changes and new mechanics is quite extensive. These changes can be divided into character behavior and weapon behavior.

On the character side, we added leaning to enable players to lean around corners or perform the friendly dance by using the Q and E keys. Additionally, there is now an improved over-the-shoulder (OTS) camera when holding the right mouse button, and an aim-down-sight (ADS) mode when single-clicking RMB. This enables a more accurate aiming experience.

On the weapon side, we have implemented weapon effects such as recoil and sway, as these go hand in hand with the new attachment system. The attachment system introduces several different attachment slots, such as handguards, buttstocks, and more. Each of these attachments can have certain functionalities like flashlights, lasers, etc., and/or increase values for sway, recoil, precision, etc. Attachments are generally rare and can mostly be found in military areas, guarded by corresponding robots.

Even though we are not currently in a bug-fixing/polishing phase, there are game-breaking technical issues that need immediate attention. One such issue was found by our alpha testers (thanks to all active alpha testers!) and caused any level changes, such as base building, chopped trees, picked-up items, etc., to disappear under certain circumstances. Although it took some time to identify the cause, we discovered an in-engine limit for network packages and were able to fix the issue by splitting the packages into smaller ones.

[h2]Miscellaneous[/h2]

There are a lot of things happening on the development side that are not directly visible to players but are very important in the long run. One of these is optimization, which, if done properly, will enable more players to enjoy the game even on weaker hardware. Over the last two weeks, we gave Albington a full optimization pass. This involved merging certain infrastructural parts of the city, unifying textures and materials, and creating LOD meshes for most of the larger structures in Albington. By doing this, we were able to replace around 10,000 objects, optimize collisions, significantly reduce RAM usage, and improve GPU performance.

notes.title: Ardem - Dev Diaries #05
notes.content:
[b]Don't forget to join our Discord to always get the latest news on updates and events![/b]

[url=https://discord.gg/ardem][img]https://playardem.com/images/devdiaries/ARDEM_Steam_Store_Discord_Banner_600x100_2.png[/img][/url]

[h1]Attention, survivors![/h1]

We are finally back with the next episode of the dev diaries! As always, we are super excited to show you some of the progress that has been made over the last two weeks and provide you with some deeper insights into the development of Ardem. Let's dive in!

[h2]Art[/h2]

If you've checked out our latest announcement, you might have noticed a sneak peek of the initial 3D draft of something resembling an antenna or a tower. Indeed, we've been working on a radio tower! The tower stands approximately 170 meters tall and supports antennas originally deployed for telecommunications and broadcasting. It's situated on the highest mountain in Ardem, nestled between the west and south coasts. Some of you may have noticed an empty area atop the mountain during the playtest. What many didn't know about the tower is that it has also served as a secret monitoring station and played a significant role in the lore of Ardem.

[img]https://playardem.com/images/devdiaries/5/ARDEM_DEVDIARY_5_RadioTower_01.png[/img]

During the crisis, the military took control of the tower and established a base nearby. Yes, this means military loot! You asked for it, and here it is. The tower's size makes it highly recognizable from great distances, serving as an excellent landmark for navigation.

[img]https://playardem.com/images/devdiaries/5/ARDEM_DEVDIARY_5_RadioTower_02.png[/img]

In our next dev diary, we'll delve into more detail about what's required to enter the radio tower, how you can operate it, and even use it as your private shelter. Additionally, we'll showcase more images from inside the tower and what you can expect. Trust us, this is going to be huge!

[img]https://playardem.com/images/devdiaries/5/ARDEM_DEVDIARY_5_RadioTower_03.png[/img]

[h2]Level Design[/h2]

Let's discuss our progress in level design, where we've made significant strides over the past two weeks.

During the playtest, some of you may have noticed that the entire coastal area on the south coast isn't yet complete, leaving a sizable gap between Albington and the eastern mountains. Some spawn points even provided views of this large, empty area. To prevent these immersion-breaking gaps in the next playtest, we're focusing on finishing this area in design and preparing it for testing.

[img]https://playardem.com/images/devdiaries/5/ARDEM_DEVDIARY_5_Town_01.gif[/img]

Our first step to fill this gap is introducing a small remote village. It comprises several residential houses and is predominantly characterized by agriculture and horticulture. The presence of these resources, along with a small creek running through the village, makes it very appealing to fresh spawns looking for a safe route for their initial loot run, steering clear of Albington. However, being nestled in a small valley, the village makes it easy for players to be observed by others on the surrounding hills.

[img]https://playardem.com/images/devdiaries/5/ARDEM_DEVDIARY_5_RemoteVillage_01.png[/img]

Furthermore, in this village, we've experimented with new types of bushes featuring dense foliage. These bushes provide unarmed players with more hiding options from hostile players. They blend seamlessly with the surrounding foliage and, based on our in-game tests, offer excellent concealment opportunities.

[h2]Game Mechanics[/h2]

[h3]Environmental Effects[/h3]

On the game mechanics front, we've addressed some feedback that many players have raised, which was relatively easy for us to implement but will have a significant impact on gameplay in the next playtest. This feedback primarily revolves around three major aspects.

[b]Day and Night Cycle:[/b] We've resolved a bug that was ignoring our settings for the length of day and night in Ardem. Previously, it would consistently apply the day length to the night as well. This issue has been rectified, and we've adjusted the durations to 45 minutes of daytime and 15 minutes of nighttime. Additionally, we've artificially extended the durations of sunrise and sunset to enhance realism.

[b]Cardinal Directions: [/b]It came to our attention, thanks to your feedback, that the path of the sun didn't align with the correct cardinal directions, making it challenging to use the sun as a navigation tool. This has been rectified, and now the sun rises in the south and sets in the west. Happy navigating!

[b]Weather Durations: [/b]Some weather types, such as thunderstorms, have aesthetically pleasing visuals but excessively long durations, which impede navigation and hearing. We've implemented the ability to set the minimum and maximum durations of different weather types and have already decreased the duration of thunderstorms accordingly.

[h3]Lamps[/h3]

During the playtest, many players utilized the electricity mechanics, connecting generators to houses and using interior lights. We've given the entire system a thorough overhaul, ensuring to adjust the brightness and light color of all lamps to achieve a more realistic appearance, avoiding cases where they resembled supernovas.

[img]https://playardem.com/images/devdiaries/5/ARDEM_DEVDIARY_5_Lamps_01.gif[/img]

Additionally, we've introduced what we call "light attachment points" to all lamps in every house. These points serve as interaction spots for reattaching lamps. When you pick up a lamp from the ceiling, a corresponding attachment point in the form of cables will appear in the same location. With a lamp in hand, you can interact with these attachment points to reattach the lamp to the ceiling. This enhancement provides you with more freedom in customizing your base and allows you to take your favorite lamps with you to your shelters and bases.

[h3]Barrels[/h3]

Last but not least, we've given all liquid containers (such as barrels, water tanks, etc.) in Ardem an overhaul. We noticed that many of you were confused by barrels and similar containers that could be opened and closed but had no further functionality. To address this, we've removed the option to open and close the lids and instead integrated our existing liquid container mechanic into them.

[img]https://playardem.com/images/devdiaries/5/ARDEM_DEVDIARY_5_Barrels_01.png[/img]

This enhancement allows you to transfer liquids like water or fuel from bottles or other smaller containers into barrels, water tanks, etc., allowing you to collect large quantities of certain liquids. This feature can be particularly useful for shelters or bases that lack easy access to a river or lake, as you can now conveniently store your water on site.

[b]While this dev diary covered numerous smaller improvements and features, rest assured that we have some major developments to showcase in the next update, and we're truly excited to share them with you. Stay tuned![/b]

notes.title: Ardem - Dev Diaries #04
notes.content:
[b]Don't forget to join our Discord to always get the latest news on updates and events![/b]

[url=https://discord.gg/ardem][img]https://playardem.com/images/devdiaries/ARDEM_Steam_Store_Discord_Banner_600x100_2.png[/img][/url]

[h1]Attention, survivors![/h1]

Survivors, it's time for the 4th episode of the Ardem Dev Diaries. As always, we are super excited to show you some of the progress that has been made over the last two weeks and provide you with some deeper insights into the development of Ardem. Let's dive in!

[h3]Art[/h3]

On the art side, we've shifted our focus from the tunnel system to electricity-related assets. One of our upcoming major projects is integrating the electricity system into player base building. Currently, only existing buildings feature the electricity system, but in the future, players will have the ability to fully electrify their bases. They can build light switches, power sockets, and much more to make their homes more comfortable. Of course, there won't be any light without proper power production. To address this, we've implemented three sources of energy: fuel, solar, and wind, which players can use to generate power for their homes. In the image below, you can see the improvised wind wheel, one of the available power sources players can build.

[img]https://playardem.com/images/devdiaries/4/ARDEM_DEVDIARY_4_WindWheel_01.png[/img]

[h3]Level Design[/h3]

Level Design has been making good progress in the last two weeks. As we get closer to the playtest, our main focus is filling the gaps between the designed areas and Albington. This ensures a smooth transition without any blank spots, giving you easy access to Albington. Currently, we're working on a highway exit that allows entry into Albington. Designing the exit was a bit challenging, but we're satisfied with how it looks and feels. Road signs will be added later on.

[img]https://playardem.com/images/devdiaries/4/ARDEM_DEVDIARY_4_HighwayExit_01.png[/img]

The recent focus on Albington centered largely on the new tunnel system, which has made substantial progress. We've introduced additional assets to the set, allowing for cross-tunnels between the main passages. In these cross-tunnels, players can switch from one system to another, only able to crouch through them. It's a risky maneuver, but sometimes the only escape. The entire system has proven to be more complex than initially anticipated, especially when ensuring that the tunnel pieces seamlessly connect to all the different entry/exit points. However, overall, we've made good progress. The next steps involve adding proper post-processing elements to these underground tunnels, creating a dense and gritty atmosphere once you enter them.

[img]https://playardem.com/images/devdiaries/4/ARDEM_DEVDIARY_4_SewageSystem_01.gif[/img]

[h3]Game Mechanics[/h3]

Over the last two weeks, a key area of focus has been the melee system. In the previous playtest, we received some negative feedback regarding the inability to use items like baseball bats or knives. Regardless of the item held, the player character was essentially using fists. We've addressed this issue and implemented several different combat states for various objects and weapons to ensure authenticity in the fighting experience. With around 700 holdable items in our game currently, there might still be some incorrect combat states assigned to certain objects, but we eagerly await your feedback during the playtest to fine-tune this.

[img]https://playardem.com/images/devdiaries/4/ARDEM_DEVDIARY_4_Melee_01.gif[/img]

Also, due to a lot of player feedback that we have received in the last playtest, we have been working on the interaction system and the general user experience. We have changed the way of how the player interacts with most objects to hold down the interaction key instead of pressing it once and then sitting in front of your PC doing nothing while you see the animation playing. This change creates a more “involved” feeling and basically feels like you are actively doing something while chopping down a tree for example. 

The second change relates to the outlining effect on all objects. We've essentially eliminated the outlining effect and replaced it with a more subtle highlight effect that gently accentuates the targeted objects. The previous outlining effect was quite aggressive, causing discomfort, especially in darker surroundings. We're still experimenting with colors and transparency, but overall, it has been implemented and is ready for use.

[img]https://playardem.com/images/devdiaries/4/ARDEM_DEVDIARY_4_InteractionSystem_01.gif[/img]

[h3]On another note[/h3]

We have now started to assign all our resources to QA and bug fixing to prepare for the upcoming playtest that we STILL did not officially announce. Internally, we have set a date and - we promise - will announce it VERY SOON. The next dev diaries might be a bit shorter or maybe even a bit of a different format as we are now fully focusing on bug fixing.

notes.title: Ardem - Dev Diaries #03
notes.content:
[b]Don't forget to join our Discord to always get the latest news on updates and events![/b]

[url=https://discord.gg/ardem][img]https://playardem.com/images/devdiaries/ARDEM_Steam_Store_Discord_Banner_600x100_2.png[/img][/url]

[h1]Attention, survivors![/h1]

Welcome to Episode #3 of the Ardem Dev Diaries. 

We are thrilled to dive deeper into the events of the last two weeks and provide you with some intriguing insights into the development of Ardem.  This one will be a bit shorter, but still a lot has happened. Let's dive in!

[h3]Art[/h3]

Today, we will begin with art. As mentioned last time, in our new city, Albington, we wanted to explore something innovative and decided to implement a sewage canal system beneath the city. This system can be utilized by players to navigate the area without exposing themselves too much to the environment. In multiplayer, there is, of course, a high chance of encountering other players in the canal systems as well. The system will include several entry/exit points, providing players the option to reach specific places more efficiently and resurface when needed.

Following an initial concept and research phase, during which we experimented with different shapes and styles, we have now settled on a design that we believe complements our visual style and the surrounding environment quite well. The various canal parts are currently in an early stage, with level designers incorporating them into the layout of the canal system. Simultaneously, we are still working on refining them, adding details, and making adjustments on the fly.

We look forward to sharing more screenshots of the sewage canal system in the next update!

[img]https://playardem.com/images/devdiaries/3/ARDEM_DEVDIARY_3_SewageAssets_01.png[/img]

[h3]Level Design[/h3]

You will continue to hear this for some time, but Albington remains our top priority. We have transitioned from the inner-city commercial area to focus more on the residential zone, meticulously shaping all the narrow lanes and alleys that connect the houses, ensuring everything looks as authentic as possible. Currently, we are in the process of placing larger props such as vehicles and sheds, as well as laying out structures like fences and walls that separate the properties. Overall, the progress in Albington is promising, and soon we will be showcasing much more.

[img]https://playardem.com/images/devdiaries/3/ARDEM_DEVDIARY_3_Albington_01.png[/img]

Additionally, we have decided against the idea of having a quarry as the local industry for Albington. Instead, we have started drafting plans for a hydrocarbon production plant, which will serve as the main industry branch in this city. More information on this will be provided in one of the upcoming updates. While the quarry is not entirely dismissed, it will be postponed and re-evaluated at a later stage.

We are consistently elevating the visual aesthetics of the game to ensure the environment feels authentic and harmonizes with the US Midwest setting of Ardem. An initiative taken over the past two weeks focused on refining the vegetation, especially in dense forests. Alongside minor adjustments to the density of grass and undergrowth, we also replaced the majority of previously used ferns. Although this might appear as a minor alteration, it significantly influences the overall ambiance of the forests. 

[img]https://playardem.com/images/devdiaries/3/ARDEM_DEVDIARY_3_Flora_01.png[/img]

As we are also proceeding to work on the more rural areas that are leading up to Albington, we recently finished an important intersection that connects both the highway and the sawmill to Albington. Besides some trailer park-ish style, the intersection consists of a burned down gas station, a diner and a motel. A decent combo of buildings for some nice loot. As the intersection is quite close to the shore, we are expecting this place to be a good starting point for fresh spawns to gather some useful early loot and then be able to head more inlands.

[img]https://playardem.com/images/devdiaries/3/ARDEM_DEVDIARY_3_Intersection_01.png[/img]

[h3]Game Mechanics[/h3]

On the game mechanics front, we have focused on the initial phase of the cooking system. This phase essentially involves grilling various foods over an open fire to transition them into a cooked state, making them more nutritious than in their raw form. It's crucial to note that leaving the food on the fire for too long after reaching the cooked state may result in it getting burned, rendering it inedible. Currently, various types of meat and grown vegetables can be placed on the grill for cooking. However, it's essential to have a proper grill grate to support the food.

In the next stage, we plan to introduce the option for players to cook individual pieces of food on a stick by holding them over the fire, especially in the absence of a grill grate. Since sticks can be found virtually everywhere, this provides a practical way to cook food without requiring advanced gear.

notes.title: Ardem - Dev Diaries #02
notes.content:
[b]Don't forget to join our Discord to always get the latest news on updates and events![/b]

[url=https://discord.gg/ardem][img]https://media.discordapp.net/attachments/515875112915042304/1195888814011465748/ARDEM_Steam_Store_Discord_Banner_600x100_2.png?ex=65b5a13f&is=65a32c3f&hm=9dc598f68b4e2fe3bb03962c671a6cc619c152454143531f0896ae68168d79d6&=&format=webp&quality=lossless[/img][/url]

[h1]Attention, survivors![/h1]

Welcome to Episode #2 of the Ardem Dev Diaries. We are thrilled to dive deeper into the events of the last two weeks and provide you with some intriguing insights into the development of Ardem. Also we will move the dev diary to Sunday instead of Saturday to allow ourselves more time to work on the report. Let's dive in!

[h2]Level Design[/h2]

One of our top priorities remains Albington, our second city. Last week, we successfully completed the infrastructure phase and transitioned into the detail phase. Here, we began placing smaller props to make the environment feel authentic. As shown in the picture, significant progress has been made, and the inner city is beginning to take shape.

We've also decided to introduce something special and new to Albington by constructing a sewer system beneath the city. This system will feature several entrance/exit points, serving as strategic elements to avoid enemies or set up ambushes. We can't wait to see players utilize this in the next playtest. More details on the sewer system will be provided in our next dev diary.

Creating a city like Albington, making it feel authentic, and populating it with loot is a task that spans several months. However, walking through the city with the team after each iteration is truly amazing.

[img]https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1195800831623184425/1201262278046121984/Albington.png?ex=65c92dad&is=65b6b8ad&hm=28b8d6653e7d24863c6fae2a577b4ec2d9ad68ab4ef17aefde2ffe43a80c3a9b&[/img]

[img]https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1195800831623184425/1201262323487219792/Albington2.png?ex=65c92db8&is=65b6b8b8&hm=de6d318c833c76d30378b46d0bc94e257de86ca31fbe03c23e6a0e61b9332ae3&[/img]

As we continue populating the landscape with various points of interest, we are also working on the roads connecting them. Due to lore reasons, we've decided that roads and highways on the south coast suffer from more overgrowth, with more vehicles and military checkpoints obstructing them, sometimes leading to significant traffic jams. On one hand, this means you need to be cautious and drive slower at certain passages (beware of ambushes). On the other hand, it provides you with more loot when you decide to explore these vehicle wrecks. Overall, we've completed the design of a large portion of the highway that leads directly to Albington.

[img]https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1195800831623184425/1201263043292709014/highway.gif?ex=65c92e63&is=65b6b963&hm=f79bfad3d0aae618e9c9d4f20fc959c83305e1745413b2f4d2a81fe87130795c&[/img]

As promised in our last dev diary, let us provide you with more details on the sawmill we've been working on. We've made significant progress on this new point of interest and almost completed the polishing phase. While a few assets, particularly the roofs, are still in the whitebox stage, we are extremely satisfied with the results and are on the verge of adding loot spawn markers to the location.

[img]https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1195800831623184425/1201263147168829590/Sawmill.png?ex=65c92e7c&is=65b6b97c&hm=47233afe63bfd21f60fbe3e3dc78313956f2f133dff89f69b776c133c1d29aea&[/img]

[h2]Game Mechanics[/h2]

On the game mechanics side, we have finally implemented a pickup notification system that displays a message on the top left screen, showing you what you've picked up and the new quantity of that item in your inventory. This feature proves especially useful for gathering crafting resources, allowing you to know your inventory contents without the need to open it. During playtests, it emerged as a significant quality-of-life improvement in Ardem.

[img]https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1195800831623184425/1201263690729664562/output-opt.gif?ex=65c92efe&is=65b6b9fe&hm=596d2310d3d4a64c79c9d6ef64b5621c2b6cd00c3c040c01ed711d48e8eee84f&[/img]

As mentioned in the last dev diary, we successfully completed and polished the bow and arrow system, conducting extensive tests and addressing any issues related to the system. Additionally, we've made smaller improvements, such as arrows sticking in animals or other players.

During our testing phase, we observed that tracking the arrow's trajectory can be challenging at times. To address this, we've added a feature to the arrow, creating a subtle "tail" behind it to visually indicate its path. Players can choose to deactivate this feature if they prefer a more challenging experience. Overall, we are highly satisfied with the new system; the shooting experience is excellent, and it introduces an additional method for obtaining food in the wilderness.

[img]https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/1195800831623184425/1201264023480578128/huntingbow.gif?ex=65c92f4d&is=65b6ba4d&hm=2b6549bfed0bad6a9ce535c86ebb4a439f898adeee7cadc66d3fa2bf95671b7a&[/img]

As we progress with implementing and balancing AI enemies, providing proper hit feedback becomes increasingly crucial for the player. We have now implemented a system to visualize received damage through a typical temporary screen effect, turning your screen red. This effect also serves as an indicator of the damage magnitude you've incurred. For instance, minor damage from punches will only cause the screen edges to fade to red, while major damage from firearms will momentarily fade the entire screen. Although the system requires further testing and polishing, it is expected to be finalized next week.

[h2]Miscellaneous[/h2]

Following our Open Alpha playtest in October 2023, we observed that a significant number of players were utilizing low-to-medium hardware and experiencing issues with low framerates, even when using lower graphics settings. As we approach the upcoming playtest, we have initiated an initial optimization pass to ensure that more players can enjoy Ardem with high settings, even on less powerful hardware. Currently, our focus is on addressing the most accessible optimization opportunities, and we have already achieved up to a 25% increase in frame rates in certain areas.

[h2][b]Attention, survivors! [/b][/h2]

Welcome to the very first episode of the Ardem Dev Diaries. In this new biweekly format, we will provide you with exciting insights into the game's development, shedding more light on what the team has been working on. Please note that we will cover a selection of things we have been working on, and there might be additional aspects that didn't make it into this report. Let's dive in!

[h3]Level Design[/h3]

After polishing the west coast of the map and fixing numerous bugs, we shifted our focus back to the south coast, where we began drafting the second city, Albington. It is expected to be roughly twice the size of Ottsburg, the city featured in the playtest, and will include exciting points of interest such as a local high school and a large quarry. Albington is currently in the infrastructure phase, where we define terrain details, street layouts, and building positions.

[img]https://media.discordapp.net/attachments/1110191469932847208/1195849672036732989/Prasentation2.png?ex=65b57ccb&is=65a307cb&hm=65668067b6cdb203b4156165cd4f771189617898d500621ff64653c7ff83ed90&=&format=webp&quality=lossless&width=1609&height=905[/img]

Additionally, we've been working on a cargo harbor, which has nearly completed the design pipeline and awaits the placement of loot spawn markers. As the cargo harbor is close to a medium-sized sawmill and used to provide urgently needed tools and spare parts, expect some valuable industrial loot! More updates on the sawmill coming in the next report.

[img]https://media.discordapp.net/attachments/1110191469932847208/1195849670866501742/Prasentation3.png?ex=65b57ccb&is=65a307cb&hm=c70de6f6a4c4b3d71fb0eba7cbea9e7a475de1e4240839fbfd6f068dc47a17b6&=&format=webp&quality=lossless&width=1609&height=905[/img]

[h3]Game Mechanics[/h3]

Addressing feedback from the open alpha playtest, we have significantly reduced the animation length for pickup and tree-processing. Despite dissatisfaction with the current animation length by a lot of users, we plan to offer multiple configuration parameters for both players and server owners to customize their user experience.

Furthermore, we have begun work on the bow-and-arrow system, confident of completing the implementation next week. This system includes shooting from standing and crouching positions, taking your stamina into account. Prolonged bow drawing will drain stamina, causing the character's arm to shiver and significantly reducing accuracy. Different bows will possess varying attributes such as impact force or max range. Despite minor animation and camera issues, we are pleased with the results and look forward to seeing you try it out in the next playtest.

[img]https://media.discordapp.net/attachments/515875112915042304/1195889608987262976/20240113_Ardem_GIF_BowArrow_01.gif?ex=65b5a1fd&is=65a32cfd&hm=dc6d64d6bb0fda17605c148bf0b7d1cf2b748bfa730ad0b100811b51ca2aed42&=[/img]

[h3]AI[/h3]

AI is a crucial focus for us in the upcoming playtest, encompassing two main groups: wild animal AI and hostile robot AI. Over the last two weeks, our focus has primarily been on wild animals, yielding positive results.

Although we implemented basic AI for wild animals some time ago, it wasn't multiplayer-ready until recently. Now, wild animals roam the map, either solo or in different-sized herds, depending on the animal. All animals follow a basic needs system, prompting them to visit places for drinking, eating, sleeping, or exploring. Additionally, animals can be killed with guns, bows, or melee, and gutted for specific resources. The next steps for implementation involve adjustments to animations and addressing edge case behaviors like killing the herd leader or fleeing.

[img]https://media.discordapp.net/attachments/515875112915042304/1195889613437423727/20240113_Ardem_GIF_AI_01.gif?ex=65b5a1fe&is=65a32cfe&hm=8108f13a4ba440a8dbb4366df12b9ab778581965f21be5d0131563322b4a0804&=[/img]

If there are specific topics you'd like us to cover in future dev diaries, please let us know!

notes.title: Patchnotes for Regular Update 0.2.4196
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

We would like to thank you for your tireless feedback, suggestions, requests, and the countless bug reports that have reached us.

After this Open Alpha and your great feedback, we are sure that the current direction of Ardem will find a large fanbase, and we have collected many valuable suggestions that we will gradually implement into the game.

notes.title: Get ready for the Ardem open alpha!
notes.content:
Hello, Survivors!

We want to start by apologizing for any confusion our latest announcement might have caused. Right now, we're hard at work testing Ardem internally, and it's important to note that the open alpha is [b]not[/b] yet live.

But here's the good news – we're making fantastic progress, and we're feeling confident that we'll be launching the open alpha in October.

We've got some details to share with you already:

[list]
[*] In the open alpha, you'll have the option to dive into singleplayer sessions or hop onto online servers.
[*] Cooperative play won't be available in the open alpha, but we promise it's getting some extra polish.
[*] We'll be providing servers for both Europe and the US, each with room for up to 32 players.
[*] During the open alpha, we'll be turning off AI because it still needs a bit of fine-tuning.
[/list]
So, we're reaching out to you and asking for a little favor – please spread the word to your friends and have them add the game to their [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2179480/Ardem/#game_area_purchase]wishlists[/url]. Also, don't forget to join our [url=https://discord.gg/ardem]Discord community[/url]. We'd love to have as many players as possible join the open alpha and provide us with their valuable feedback. 

Thanks for being awesome!

notes.title: Ardem v0.2.2907 now live for all testers!
notes.content:
[h2]Greetings, Testers![/h2]

A big "Thank You" to all those who consistently reported issues. Your help and support mean the world to us, and we're happy to announce that the next update is ready to roll out today. Our team has poured their efforts into enhancing the current content and introducing new features to the game. Let's delve into the specifics of what this update entails.

[h3]User Interface[/h3]
We've been fine-tuning Ardem's menu system. As the game evolves and we gear up for Steam Next Fest, we're rolling out a comprehensive menu revamp. Expect a sleek new main menu that captures the essence of Ardem, alongside essential submenus for options, keybindings, and more. Oh, and no more ALT+F4 exit routine. We've streamlined things with an in-game menu (ESC), ensuring a smoother transition within the gameplay experience.

[h3]Fishing[/h3]
Fishing is now in the game. Equip your fishing rod and venture to lakes, rivers, or the vast ocean to test your fishing skills. Watch closely as the floater dips and your fishing line moves. Press the F key at the right moment to hook your catch. We're now proceedind to ramping up the system, soon introducing different baits that attract various types of fish.

[h3]Lootspawn[/h3]
We've finally implemented random lootspawn! Right now, loot is plentiful everywhere, but we're working on fine-tuning it for a more balanced experience. Expect urban areas and structures to be rich with loot while more rural or even foresty areas are rather poor with loot. We are also actively working on a lot of crafting receipes that will consume your hard-earned loot.

[h3]Southcoast[/h3]
Our level designers have been tirelessly working on the Southcoast region, continuing to work on a vast new expanse. Additionally, we're excited to introduce a captivating new point of interest – the 'Sawmill,' now prominently featured on the main map in the southcoast region. While a few whitebox elements remain visible, feel free to explore the area and provide us with some valuable feedback regarding its aesthetics and ambiance.

[h3]Bugfixes:[/h3]

[list]
[*] Fixed a server crash when a player was building a basebuilding piece 
[*] Fixed a server crash when container inventory unloaded on client
[*] Fixed an issue where the player would spawn without spawn gear
[*] Fixed an issue when the player character rolled into water
[*] Fixed an issue where certain items could be picked up infinately
[*] Fixed an issue where you would get stuck in the basebuilding wheel input mode
[*] Fixed an issue where items would not stack when dragged from a container
[*] Fixed an issue where items from a container would ignore the players inventory space
[*] Fixed the wrong size of edible mushrooms to a more realistic size
[*] Fixed an issue where melee fight mode could be activated during sprint
[*] Fixed an issue where the player was moving a flashlight into its head during run
[*] Fixed missing upgrade options for roof overhang piece
[*] Fixed missing upgrade options for sunroof corner piece
[*] Fixed an issue where the engine repair animation got stuck in an endless loop
[*] Fixed a weird hand movement when consuming a mushroom
[*] Fixed smaller UI issues with wrong indicators after relog
[*] Fixed the bug report UI not removing the previous descriptions
[*] Fixed an issue where basebuilding placement shaders would not disappear
[*] Fixed missing placement shaders for Jerry Can
[*] Fixed the vehicle horn not having attenuation settings
[*] Fixed around 50 Leveldesign related issues
[/list]
